subject: Day 30: carrier walk outside
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 30 days old and near the peak of the PURPLE crying curve, where inconsolable evenings are normal across cultures and feeding methods. Today's lever is a carrier walk outdoors: upright, motion, and fresh sensory input tend to settle a fussy infant better than any device.

Action items
- Take a 20 to 30 minute carrier walk this afternoon with Avi facing in, chin off his chest and face visible so the airway stays open; motion plus your heartbeat is one of the most reliable settling tools at this age. AAP HealthyChildren: Movement, Birth to 3 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Confirm the 1-month visit is complete with growth and feeding tracking logged; if anything was deferred, close it out this week.
- Keep the 5 S's in rotation for the evening cluster (swaddle, side-hold, shush, swing, suck); about 80 to 90 percent of infants calm to some combination. AAP HealthyChildren: Crying and Colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Inconsolable crying in the evenings with no clear cause; PURPLE crying is a normal developmental phase, not a pathology, and peaks around six weeks.
- [monitor] Crying exceeding 3 hours a day, 3 days a week, for 3 weeks meets the Wessel definition of colic; document the pattern but coping strategies matter more than the label.
- [call within 24h] Forceful arching during or after feeds with frequent painful spit-up and feed refusal despite hunger cues, suggesting GERD or cow's-milk-protein intolerance.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, blue color around the lips, labored breathing, or seizure-like activity; for blue lips call 911 and do not second-guess it.

Enrichment opportunities
- Carry Avi outdoors in the carrier with his face visible and chin off his chest; upright motion delivers vestibular and visual input that floor time cannot, and tends to defuse the evening fuss. AAP HealthyChildren: Movement, Birth to 3 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Coo back and forth as you walk: respond to each sound he makes, pause two to three seconds, then respond again. Conversational turns, not raw word count, predict later language-related brain function. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns and brain function: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Hum a steady walking tune the whole route; live participatory voice, not recorded background music, is the active ingredient in early musical engagement. Gerry et al. 2012, active music classes in infancy: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/

Upcoming
- Day 35-41 (around week 6): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit; OB will cover pelvic floor, mood screen, contraception, and exercise clearance.
- Day 56-70 (2-month well visit): vaccines due are HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1.
- Day 57-72 (post-vaccine window): expect fussiness, low-grade fever, and drowsiness for 24 to 48 hours after the 2-month shots.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
